p.src: Your younger sister Tanchun respectfully addresses her second brother at his writing desk: The evening before last, after the skies had newly cleared and the moonlight seemed freshly washed, I could not bear to retire and lose so rare a scene. Though the water clock had already sounded the third watch, I still lingered beneath the paulownia balustrade; caught unawares by wind and dew, I consequently fell ill. Yesterday you graciously came in person to comfort and advise me, then repeatedly sent maids to inquire after me; moreover, you bestowed fresh lychees and a specimen of Yan Zhenqing’s calligraphy. How deeply your loving concern touches one in affliction! Now, as I lean over my desk or rest against my bed in quiet seclusion, I reflect that men of old, even amid the field where fame was contested and profit fought over, would still establish some little retreat of hill and stream. Summoning distant friends and welcoming those nearby, detaining their carriages and clinging to their shafts, they strove to gather two or three kindred spirits to sojourn there. Some raised an altar of letters, others founded poetry clubs; though born of a passing impulse, these became cherished tales for a thousand ages. Though I lack talent, I too have had the privilege of dwelling amid springs and rocks, and I also admire the gifts of Xue Tao and Xie Daoyun. Courtyards of wind and terraces of moonlight sadly lack a gathering of poets; amid curtained apricot blossoms and peach-lined streams, perhaps cups of inspiration might fly in tipsy merriment. Who says the lofty talents of the Lotus Society may belong only to bearded men, or that the elegant gathering on the Eastern Hills must be yielded entirely to them by us women? If you will honor me by rowing here through the snow, I shall sweep away the fallen flowers and await you. Respectfully submitted.

p.src: Your unworthy son Yun respectfully wishes his honored father every blessing and golden peace. Ever since Heaven blessed me by allowing me to be acknowledged as your son, I have thought day and night of showing you filial devotion, yet have found no opportunity to do so. Previously, while purchasing flowers and plants, thanks to your good fortune watching over me, I became acquainted with many gardeners and learned of many famous gardens. I happened then to see a rare variety of white begonia. After trying every possible means, I managed to obtain only two pots. If you regard me as you would your own son, please keep them for your enjoyment. As the weather is hot and I feared my entering the garden might inconvenience the young ladies, I did not dare present myself in person. I respectfully submit this letter and again inquire after your honored well-being. Your son Yun writes this on his knees.

p.src: When they saw him enter, they all laughed and said, “Here comes another one.” Tanchun laughed. “I cannot be called entirely commonplace. A notion happened to strike me, so I wrote a few invitations to see what would happen—and one summons has brought everyone here.” Baoyu laughed. “It is a pity we waited so long. We should have founded a club ages ago.” Daiyu said, “Go ahead and found your club, but do not count me in. I would never dare join.” Yingchun laughed. “If you do not dare, who else possibly could?” Baoyu said, “This is a serious undertaking. Everyone must enter into it with enthusiasm, without all this mutual modesty. Whatever ideas you have, put them forward freely so that we can all consider them. Sister Bao, offer us an idea, and Sister Lin, say something too.” Baochai said, “Why are you in such a hurry? Not everyone is here yet.” Before she had finished speaking, Li Wan arrived. Entering the room, she laughed and said, “How exceedingly elegant! If you are founding a poetry club, I volunteer to preside over it. I had this same idea myself last spring. But then I reflected that I cannot write poetry, so what business had I making a fuss? I consequently forgot the idea and never mentioned it. Since Third Sister is so enthusiastic, I shall help you make a flourishing success of it.”

p.src: Daiyu said, “Since we are determined to form a poetry club, we shall all be poets now. To avoid sounding commonplace, we must first dispense with such terms as ‘sister,’ ‘cousin,’ and ‘sister-in-law.’” Li Wan said, “Quite right. Why should we not each choose a literary name and address one another by those? It would be much more elegant. I have settled on ‘Old Farmer of Sweet-Rice Village,’ which no one else can claim.” Tanchun laughed. “Then I shall be ‘The Recluse of Autumn Freshness.’” Baoyu said, “‘Recluse’ and ‘Mistress’ do not quite suit you, and the name is cumbersome besides. There are plenty of parasol trees and plantains here; a name derived from one of those would be better.” Tanchun laughed. “I have it! Since I am especially fond of plantains, I shall call myself ‘Guest beneath the Plantain.’” Everyone agreed that the name was novel and amusing. Daiyu laughed. “Quick, lead her away, stew her into venison, and serve her with wine.” No one understood her. Daiyu explained with a laugh, “The ancients spoke of ‘a plantain leaf covering a deer.’ Since she calls herself ‘Guest beneath the Plantain,’ does that not make her a deer? Hurry and make venison of her.” At this, everyone burst out laughing. Tanchun laughed. “Do not be so quick to turn a clever phrase against me. I have already thought of a splendid name that suits you perfectly.” Then she said to the others, “Long ago, the tears shed by the imperial consorts Ehuang and Nüying stained the bamboo, which is why mottled bamboo is also called ‘Xiang Consort Bamboo.’ Now she lives in Xiaoxiang Lodge and is forever weeping. Someday, when she pines for her husband, Master Lin, all those bamboos will surely become mottled too. From now on, we need only call her ‘Consort of the Xiaoxiang.’” Everyone clapped and acclaimed the name as marvelous. Lin Daiyu lowered her head and said nothing. Li Wan laughed. “I have long since thought of a good name for Cousin Xue too, and it consists of only three characters.” Xichun and Yingchun both asked what it was. Li Wan said, “I would bestow on her the title ‘Mistress of Alpinia.’ What do you all think?” Tanchun laughed. “That is an excellent title.” Baoyu asked, “And what about me? You must think of one for me too.” Baochai laughed. “You already have a name: the three characters ‘Busy Doing Nothing’ suit you perfectly.” Li Wan said, “You had better keep your old name, ‘Lord of the Flowers in Crimson Cavern.’” Baoyu laughed. “That was childish business. Why bring it up again?” Tanchun said, “You have more names than enough already. Why choose another? Whatever we choose to call you, you need only answer.” Baochai said, “Still, let me give you a name. There is one exceedingly commonplace name that suits you better than any other. Wealth and rank are rare in this world, and leisure is rare as well; rarer still is it for anyone to possess both. Yet, unexpectedly, you do. So we may as well call you ‘The Wealthy and Honored Idler.’” Baoyu laughed. “I am unworthy of it, quite unworthy. You may all call me whatever you please.”

p.src: Li Wan said, “Yes, that will do nicely. But as I am the eldest, you must all follow my proposal. I guarantee it will please everyone. There are seven of us forming the club, but the Second and Fourth Young Ladies and I cannot write poetry, so the three of us should be excused from that duty. Instead, each of us three will undertake one task.” Tanchun laughed. “Now that we have literary names, if we go on addressing one another as before, we might as well not have chosen them. We ought to establish a penalty for anyone who makes that mistake from now on.” Li Wan said, “Once the club is formally established, we shall set the penalties. My place is spacious, so let us hold the meetings there. Although I cannot write poetry, if all these poets do not object to a vulgar guest, I shall act as hostess and naturally acquire some refinement myself. If you choose me as president, one president alone will clearly not suffice, so we must appoint two vice-presidents as well. Let us invite the two learned scholars Caltrop Islet and Lotus Pavilion: one can set the topic and prescribe the rhyme, while the other copies out the poems and supervises the session. Nor should there be a rigid rule that the three of us may never compose. If we encounter an easier topic and rhyme, we may write a poem as we please. But the four of you must be bound by the rules. If you agree to these terms, we shall form the club; if you do not, I dare not presume to join such gifted company.” Yingchun and Xichun were naturally disinclined to compose poetry, and with Xue Baochai and Lin Daiyu before them, this proposal accorded perfectly with their wishes. Both said, “Quite right.” Tanchun and the others understood their feelings. Seeing that the two were pleased and convinced, they could hardly force them and had no choice but to agree. Tanchun laughed. “Very well, then. Still, when I think about it, it is rather amusing: I came up with this fine idea, only to have the three of you take charge of me.” Baoyu said, “In that case, let us go to Sweet-Rice Village now.” Li Wan said, “You are always so impatient. Today we are merely discussing matters; wait until I invite you properly.” Baochai said, “We should also decide how often to meet.” Tanchun said, “If we meet too often, it will cease to be enjoyable. Two or three times a month would be best.” Baochai nodded. “Twice a month will be enough.” They would set fixed dates and meet without fail, whatever the wind or rain. Apart from those two days, if anyone was in the mood and wished to arrange an extra meeting, whether at her own residence or by joining it onto another gathering, that too would be permitted. Would that not make the club livelier and more enjoyable? Everyone said, “That is an even better idea.”

p.src: Tanchun said, “Since the idea was originally mine, I must first play host, or I should be unworthy of my own enthusiasm.” Li Wan said, “In that case, why not hold the first meeting tomorrow?” Tanchun said, “Today is better than tomorrow; this very moment will do splendidly. You may set the topic, Lingzhou choose the rhymes, and Ouxie supervise the contest.” Yingchun said, “In my opinion, we need not let any one person set the topic and prescribe the rhymes. Drawing lots would be fairer.” Li Wan said, “As I came just now, I saw them carrying in two pots of white begonias. They were lovely flowers. Why not compose poems about them?” Yingchun said, “We have not even admired them yet, and already we are to write poems about them?” Baochai said, “They are only white begonias. Why must we see them before composing? The poems and rhapsodies of the ancients were, after all, merely means of giving expression to inspiration and feeling. Had they always waited until they saw their subjects, we would not have all those poems today.” Yingchun said, “Very well, then. Let me prescribe the rhymes.” So saying, she went to the bookshelf, drew out a volume of poetry, and opened it at random. The poem she found happened to be a regulated verse of seven-character lines. She passed it around for everyone to see, and thus they were all to compose seven-character regulated verse. Yingchun closed the book and said to a young maid, “Say the first character that comes into your head.” The girl was leaning against the doorway, so she said the character “door.” Yingchun laughed. “Then we shall rhyme on ‘door’—the Thirteenth Yuan rhyme group. The first rhyme must be this character ‘door.’” She then had the box of rhyme tablets brought over, pulled out the drawer marked “Thirteenth Yuan,” and told the little maid to take four tablets at random. The girl drew the four tablets “pot,” “soul,” “trace,” and “dusk.” Baoyu said, “Those two characters, ‘pot’ and ‘door,’ will not be easy to use!”

If inspiration takes you between those dates, you may choose another day and hold an extra meeting. You may meet every day of the month for all I care; I shall not interfere. But on the second and sixteenth, you must all come to my place.” Baoyu said, “But surely we must give the club a name.” Tanchun said, “A commonplace name would be no good, but neither would one so novel as to be strained and eccentric. Since crab-apple poems happened to begin our activities, why not call it the Crab-Apple Poetry Club? p.src: Now Xiren had seen Baoyu read the note and then hurry off in a fluster with Cuimo, but she had no idea what the matter was. Later, she saw two old women from the rear gate deliver two pots of crab-apple flowers. When Xiren asked where they had come from, one of the women explained what had previously passed with Baoyu. Since you happen to be here, go out on your way and tell the boys at the rear gate to hire a cart. When they return, have them come here for the money; there is no need to let them blunder about in the front part of the compound again.” The women assented and left.

p.src: Xiren returned to the room to fetch a dish in which to put the things for Shi Xiangyun, but saw that one of the plate slots in the partition shelf was empty. Turning around, she saw Qingwen, Qiuwen, Sheyue, and the others sewing together, and asked, “Where has that white agate dish with the twisted-thread pattern gone?” At the question, they all looked at one another, but none could remember. After a while, Qingwen laughed and said, “It was used to take lychees to Third Miss, and it has not been sent back yet.” Xiren said, “We have plenty of ordinary vessels for sending things. Why go especially out of the way to use that one?” Qingwen replied, “Didn’t I say the very same thing? She said that fresh lychees would look best on that dish. When I took them over, Third Miss also said how pretty they looked and told me to leave the dish with them, so I did not bring it back. And look: the pair of conjoined-pearl vases from the very top of the shelf have not come back either.” Qiuwen laughed. “Speaking of those vases reminds me of something amusing. Once our Second Master Bao’s filial feelings are stirred, he carries his devotion to the utmost degree. The other day, he saw the osmanthus blooming in the garden and cut two sprigs, intending at first to arrange them in vases for himself. Then he suddenly reflected that these were newly opened, fresh flowers from his own garden and that he ought not to enjoy them first. So he went especially to take down that pair of vases, filled them with water, arranged the flowers himself, had someone carry them, and personally presented one vase to the Old Lady and the other to Lady Wang. Who would have thought that when his filial feelings were stirred, even the servant accompanying him would share in the blessing? As it happened, I was the one who carried the flowers that day. The Old Lady was beside herself with delight when she saw them and told everyone she met, ‘Baoyu truly is devoted to me—he even remembers me when he has a single sprig of flowers. And yet the others do nothing but complain that I dote on him.’ You know that the Old Lady does not usually speak to me much, since I do not altogether please her. But that day she actually had someone give me several hundred cash, saying that I was a poor dear, so slight and delicate. That was a piece of good fortune I could never have expected. The few hundred cash were a small matter; what was precious was the honor she showed me. When I reached Lady Wang’s rooms, she, Second Mistress Lian, Concubine Zhao, Concubine Zhou, and several others were rummaging through chests, looking for some brightly colored clothes Lady Wang had worn in her youth, though I do not know whom they meant to give them to. The moment they saw the flowers, they stopped looking for the clothes and turned their attention to them instead. Second Mistress Lian was there too, making much of the occasion and praising Baoyu for being so filial and so sensible, piling up cartloads of remarks both relevant and irrelevant. Before everyone present, Lady Wang felt that this enhanced her own credit and silenced any criticism from the others. Lady Wang grew more delighted than ever and rewarded me on the spot with two of the ready-made garments. The clothes themselves were no great matter—I receive some every year in any case—but that was nothing like the auspicious honor of receiving them on such an occasion.” Qingwen laughed. “Pah!”

p.src: You ignorant little wretch! They gave the best things to someone else and only handed you what was left, yet you still have the face to boast about it.” Qiuwen said, “No matter who had first choice, it was still Madam’s kindness.” Qingwen said, “If it were me, I would not take it. It would be different if I were merely given something left over from another person. We all serve in the same room; how can one of us be nobler than another? If she gave the best to her and only the leftovers to me, I would sooner go without. Even if it meant offending Madam, I would not swallow such a slight.” Qiuwen hurriedly asked, “Who in this room was given some? I was ill for several days recently and went home, so I do not know who it was. Dear sister, please tell me so that I may know.” Qingwen said, “If I tell you, will you return it to Madam at once?” Qiuwen laughed. “Nonsense! I merely want to hear it for my own amusement. Even if it was left over by the dog in this room, I acknowledge only Madam’s kindness and have no wish to meddle in anything else.” Everyone laughed on hearing this. “What a clever way to scold her! Was it not given to that little foreign speckled lapdog?” Xiren laughed. “You foul-mouthed lot! Whenever you have a spare moment, you make me the butt of your jokes. Who knows what sort of death awaits each of you?” Qiuwen laughed. “So it was you who received them, sister. I truly did not know. Let me apologize.” Xiren laughed. “Enough of your nonsense. One of you had better go and fetch the dish.” Sheyue said, “We should also bring that vase back when we have a chance. It would be safe enough in the Old Lady’s quarters, but there are too many people coming and going in Madam’s rooms. The others might be harmless, but when Aunt Zhao’s people see that it belongs to this room, they will maliciously damage it before they are satisfied. Madam pays little attention to such things, so we had better retrieve it soon.” At this, Qingwen threw down her needlework and said, “That is true. I will go and fetch it.” Qiuwen said, “Let me fetch it. You go and get your dish.” Qingwen laughed. “No, I am determined to go this once. You have all had your lucky turns; am I not allowed one too?” Sheyue laughed. “All that happened was that Qiuwen once received some clothes. What fresh stroke of luck do you expect today? Do you think you will find them looking for clothes again?” Qingwen sneered. “Even if I find no clothes, perhaps Madam will notice how diligent I am and allot me two taels of silver each month from her household allowance. You never know.” Then she added with a laugh, “Do not play your mysterious tricks on me. There is nothing I do not know.” Still speaking, she ran outside. Qiuwen went out with her, then made her own way to Tanchun’s quarters to fetch the dish.

p.src: When Xiren had made everything ready, she summoned an old serving woman named Song from their quarters and said to her, “Wash and comb yourself properly first, then put on your outdoor clothes. I am sending you now to deliver some things to Miss Shi.” Nanny Song said, “Just entrust them to me, miss, and tell me any message you have. Once I am ready, I can deliver everything in a single trip.” Hearing this, Xiren brought over two small cloisonné boxes. She opened the first, which contained two kinds of fresh fruit, red water chestnuts and fox nuts. The other held a dish of cakes made from fresh chestnut flour, sugar, and sweet osmanthus, steamed together. She continued, “These are all newly ripened fruits from our garden this year. Second Master Bao sends them for you to taste, miss. And since you said the other day that you liked this agate dish, please keep it to enjoy. Inside this silk bundle is the needlework you asked me to do the other day. Please excuse its roughness and use it if you can. Give her our respects, and convey Second Master’s greetings. That is all.” Nanny Song said, “Second Master Bao may have something else to say. You had better ask him, miss, lest he complain when I return that we forgot.” Xiren therefore asked Qiuwen, “Did you see him just now at Third Miss’s place?” Qiuwen replied, “They were all there discussing the formation of some poetry club and composing poems. I expect he has no message. You may simply go.” On hearing this, Nanny Song took the things outside and changed her clothes. Xiren reminded her once more, “Leave by the back gate. A servant boy and a carriage are waiting there.” After Nanny Song departed, nothing further need be said of her journey.

p.src: When Baoyu returned, he first hurried to admire the crab flowers for a while, then went to his room and told Xiren about the founding of the poetry club. Xiren, in turn, told Baoyu that she had sent Nanny Song to deliver some things to Shi Xiangyun. Hearing this, Baoyu clapped his hands. “Of all people, I forgot her! I kept feeling there was something I had to remember, but I could not think what it was. Thank goodness you mentioned her—I was just about to invite her. What pleasure would there be in the poetry club without her?” Xiren advised him, “It is nothing important, merely an amusement. She is not as free as all of you and cannot decide matters for herself at home. If you tell her, she may wish to come but have no power to do so; and if she cannot come, she will pine for it. There is no need to make her unhappy.” Baoyu said, “That does not matter. I will ask the Old Lady to send someone to fetch her.” As they spoke, Nanny Song returned. After conveying Miss Shi’s thanks and acknowledging Xiren’s trouble, she continued, “Miss Shi asked what Second Master was doing. I told her that he and the young ladies had formed some sort of poetry club and were composing poems. Miss Shi said that they had not even told her they were composing poems, and she was beside herself with vexation.” On hearing this, Baoyu immediately rose and went to Grandmother Jia’s quarters, where he pressed her to send someone at once to fetch Xiangyun. Grandmother Jia said, “It is already late today. We shall send for her first thing tomorrow morning.” Baoyu had no choice but to give up for the moment and returned in low spirits.

p.src: With every line they read, their astonishment increased; when they had finished, they praised the poems without cease. “These truly deserve to be called begonia poems,” they all said. “They more than justify founding a Begonia Poetry Club.” Shi Xiangyun said, “Tomorrow, let my punishment be to act as host. May I be the first to convene a meeting of the club?” “That would be better still,” the others replied. They then went over the poems of the previous day with her and discussed them one by one. That evening, Baochai invited Xiangyun to spend the night at Allspice Court. By lamplight, Xiangyun considered how she should arrange the feast and choose the poetic theme. Baochai listened to her suggestions for some time, but found none of them suitable. At last she said, “If you are going to hold a meeting of the club, you must act as host. Though it is only a pastime, you must think everything through. You need to keep the expense manageable for yourself without giving offense to anyone; only then will everyone enjoy it. You have no authority over affairs in your own household, and the few strings of cash you receive each month are scarcely enough for your own expenses. If you spend it now on something so unnecessary, your aunt will complain about you more than ever when she hears of it. Besides, even if you used all your money, it would not be enough to host such a gathering. Surely you cannot ask your family for money just for this? Or do you mean to ask for it here?” These words brought Xiangyun to her senses, and she began to hesitate. Baochai said, “I already have an idea about that. One of the assistants at our pawnshop has excellent fat crabs on his family's farm, and a few days ago he sent us several catties. Of all the people here, from the Old Lady down to those in the garden, more than half are fond of crabs. A few days ago, Mother said that she meant to invite the Old Lady into the garden to admire the osmanthus and eat crabs, but other matters have kept her from doing so. For the moment, say nothing about the poetry club and simply invite everyone to an ordinary gathering. After the others have dispersed, there will be no limit to the poems we can compose. I shall ask my brother to obtain several baskets of the largest and fattest crabs, fetch a few jars of good wine from the shop, and prepare four or five tables of fruit and side dishes. Would that not save trouble and provide everyone with a lively time?” Xiangyun was deeply impressed and grateful when she heard this, and praised Baochai highly for thinking of everything so carefully. Baochai smiled again. “I say all this out of sincere concern for you. You must not take offense and imagine that I am looking down on you, or our friendship will have been in vain. If you do not misunderstand me, I can tell them to make the arrangements.” Xiangyun hurriedly replied with a smile, “Dear sister, by saying that, it is you who are being overly considerate of my feelings. However foolish a person might be, if she could not even tell kindness from ill intent, could she still be considered human? If I did not regard you as my own elder sister, I would never have confided all those private family matters and troubles to you last time.”

p.src: Here Baochai again said to Xiangyun, “The poetry topics should not be excessively novel or ingenious. Consider those contrived and eccentric topics in the poems of the ancients, and their exceedingly difficult rhymes. If a topic is too ingenious and the rhyme too hazardous, no fine poem can result; it will always have an amateurish air. Poetry certainly suffers from hackneyed expressions, but one must not strain too hard after novelty either. The first necessity is freshness of conception; then the diction will naturally be free of vulgarity. After all, this is nothing of great importance; spinning, weaving, and needlework are the proper occupations of girls like us. When we have leisure, the proper thing is to read a few chapters of books that will truly benefit us.” Xiangyun assented, then said with a smile, “I have been thinking: yesterday we composed poems on begonias; how would it be if I composed one on chrysanthemums now?” Baochai said, “Chrysanthemums do suit the season, but too many poets before us have written about them.” Xiangyun said, “That is just what I thought. I fear we would fall into convention.” Baochai thought for a moment and said, “I have it. Let us now make the chrysanthemum the guest and the person the host, and devise several two-character topics: one abstract character and one concrete character. The concrete one will be ‘chrysanthemum,’ while the abstract one may be drawn from words of general application. In this way each poem will both celebrate the chrysanthemum and recount an action. No one before us has done it, so it cannot become conventional. It will unite the depiction of a scene with the celebration of an object, and be both fresh and dignified.” Xiangyun smiled. “That is excellent. But I do not know what sort of abstract character would be best. Think of one first and let me hear it.” Baochai thought for a moment and said with a smile, “‘Dreaming of Chrysanthemums’ would do nicely.” Xiangyun smiled. “It certainly would. I have one too. Would ‘Shadows of Chrysanthemums’ do?” Baochai said, “That will do as well. Someone has written on it before, but if we have many topics, it may be included among them. I have thought of another.” Xiangyun said, “Tell me quickly.” Baochai said, “How about ‘Questioning the Chrysanthemums’?” Xiangyun struck the table and cried that it was marvelous, then added, “I have one too. How about ‘Visiting the Chrysanthemums’?” Baochai also praised it as delightful, then said, “We may as well devise ten topics before we write them down.” As they spoke, the two ground the ink and dipped a brush; Xiangyun wrote while Baochai dictated, and before long they had made up ten topics. After looking them over, Xiangyun smiled again. “Ten do not yet make a complete set. Let us make up twelve and complete it, like the leaves in someone’s album of calligraphy and paintings.” Hearing this, Baochai thought of two more, bringing the total to twelve. Then she said, “Since we have done this much, we may as well arrange them in sequence.” Xiangyun said, “That is better still. We shall turn it into a whole chrysanthemum catalogue.”

p.src: Baochai said, “We begin with ‘Remembering Chrysanthemums.’ Since remembrance cannot bring them to us, we visit them; therefore the second is ‘Visiting Chrysanthemums.’ Having found them, we plant them; hence the third is ‘Planting Chrysanthemums.’ Once they have been planted and bloom luxuriantly, we face them and admire them; so the fourth is ‘Facing Chrysanthemums.’ When admiration face to face leaves our delight unspent, we cut them and place them in a vase for enjoyment; thus the fifth is ‘Displaying Chrysanthemums.’ If, after displaying them, we do not compose verses, the chrysanthemums themselves seem to lack color; so the sixth is ‘Celebrating Chrysanthemums.’ Once they have entered poetry, brush and ink must also be devoted to them; thus the seventh is ‘Painting Chrysanthemums.’ After all this bustling activity for the chrysanthemums, we still do not know what is so wonderful about them and cannot help asking; hence the eighth is ‘Questioning Chrysanthemums.’ If the chrysanthemums seem able to answer, our delight becomes uncontrollable; thus the ninth is ‘Wearing Chrysanthemums.’ Although human activity is thereby exhausted, aspects of the chrysanthemums remain to be celebrated: ‘Shadows of Chrysanthemums’ and ‘Dreaming of Chrysanthemums’ follow as the tenth and eleventh, while the final leaf, ‘Withered Chrysanthemums,’ gathers up and concludes the splendor of all the preceding topics. In this way we shall have all the marvelous scenes and pleasures of the three autumn months.” Following her instructions, Xiangyun copied out the topics. After looking them over once more, she asked, “What rhyme should we prescribe?” Baochai said, “I have never liked prescribed rhymes. When one plainly has the makings of a fine poem, why suffer oneself to be fettered by rhyme? Let us not imitate those petty schools. We shall set the topics but leave the rhymes unrestricted. Our purpose is merely for everyone to enjoy whatever fine lines may occur to them, not to make things difficult.” Xiangyun said, “That is quite right. Everyone’s poetry will improve all the more in that way. But there are only five of us and twelve topics. Surely each person is not expected to compose twelve poems?” Baochai said, “That would indeed be asking too much. Copy these topics out neatly, specify that all the poems are to be seven-character regulated verse, and paste the list on the wall tomorrow. After they see it, each may compose on whichever topic she chooses. Those with the ability may compose all twelve; those without it need not complete even one. Honor will go to those of greatest talent and swiftest accomplishment. Once all twelve topics have been completed, no latecomer may compose another poem afterward; we shall simply punish her, and that will be the end of it.” Xiangyun said, “That arrangement will do.” Only after the two had settled every detail did they extinguish the lamp and retire for the night. To learn what followed, listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
